name: frotz
why: A Z-machine interpreter that plays classic Infocom interactive fiction, a strange old-school environment worth a break.

brief.what_it_is: Frotz is an interpreter for Z-machine story files, the format used by Infocom's classic text adventures and many other interactive fiction games. You give it a Z-code game file and it runs the story in a terminal, taking typed commands and printing the game's text responses. The homepage at 661.org is only a directory listing of release tarballs and a zip, with no README; the project's README text came from the GitHub mirror, which points to GitLab as the live home. The package installs three executables: dfrotz, frotz, and sfrotz.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes Frotz as an interpreter for all Infocom and other Z-machine games, ported to Unix so these games can run on modern systems. It is framed as a reference implementation of Graham Nelson's Z-machine standard 1.0.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It says the program compiles on most Unix flavors, plays all Z-code games including V6, supports sound through libao, and reads config files with configurable error checking.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the README points to an INSTALL file in the source tree, which I did not read. Building from source is the documented route: the homepage offers frotz-2.44.tar.gz and the GitLab project hosts the current source. Sound output needs libao. Config files are supported. No accounts or hardware are needed. The GitLab page lists the project as GPL v2.0 or later.
brief.standout: It is a small, long-lived, portable C reimplementation of the Infocom Z-machine that still plays nearly the whole catalogue of Z-code games, including the rarely supported V6 format. The three binaries split the work: frotz for the terminal, dfrotz for dumb terminals, and sfrotz for sound output.
brief.status: Maintained, with some ambiguity. The GitLab project is the live repository, and the README names David Griffith as current maintainer. The GitHub repo says it has moved and is deprecated. The README header reads V2.45pre, while the newest tarball on the 661.org listing is frotz-2.44.tar.gz, dated 2015-May-25, and the 250.zip is dated 2019-Nov-12. I could not confirm a recent commit date from the GitLab page.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a bare file index with no description, so the README came from the GitHub mirror, which is deprecated. Frotz is GPL licensed. The README's lone point of concern is that it is a pre-release version at 2.45pre. The 661.org listing also contains stray files such as index.html.orig and index.html.redirect. The tool's brew description is terse, and I saw no installation commands in the README itself.
quotes: FROTZ V2.45pre - An interpreter for all Infocom and other Z-machine games.
Compiles and runs on most common flavors of Unix, both open source and not.
Plays all Z-code games including V6.
